chunks: From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Abdul A'ala who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Teach me an advice which I can be advised with.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'A man came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said to him, 'O Messenger of Allah, teach me an advice which I can be advised with.' So he (peace be upon him) said to him, 'Go, and do not be angry.' Then he reiterated to him, so he (peace be upon him) said to him, 'Go, and do not be angry' – three times.'

key_terms.عِظَةً: an advice / a piece of wisdom

ai.seo_question: What was the Prophet's repeated advice to the man who asked for a single piece of advice?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in al-Kafi, underscores the Prophet’s emphasis on anger management as the foundational pillar of moral character, a theme deeply resonant in Shia ethics where self-restraint (hilm) is viewed as a divine attribute. The repetition of the advice three times signifies its critical importance, suggesting that conquering anger is not merely a single act but a continuous spiritual discipline required for inner peace and social harmony. This narrative aligns with the Shia understanding of the Ahl al-Bayt’s role in preserving and elucidating the Prophet’s practical teachings on character development.

en.hubeali: From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibrahim Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Abdul A’ala who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Teach me an advice which I can be advised with’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘A man came over to Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> and he said, ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! Teach me an advice I can be advised with’. So he<sup>saww</sup> said to him: ‘Go, and don’t be angry’. Then he reiterated to him<sup>saww</sup>. So he<sup>saww</sup> said to him: ‘Go, and don’t be angry’ – three times’.
en.sarwar: 5. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from ibn Faddal from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Ash’ari from ‘Abd al-‘Ala who has said the following:

“Once I said to abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) ‘Please teach me good advice that will help me learn a lesson.’ The Imam said, ‘Once a man came to the Messenger of Allah and said, “O Messenger of Allah, teach me an advice that will help me learn a good lesson.” The Messenger of Allah said, ‘Go, but do not become angry.’ The man repeated his question the Messenger of Allah said three times, ‘Go and do not become angry.’”
